summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 136) in which a speaker describes how evolutionary computing could produce artificial intelligence: random programs are repeatedly varied and selected, and an AI could be bred by making the whole world a Turing Test, with software agents surviving human judgment in online spaces. The narrative then turns to Annalisa, who expects to be disappeared into a secret tribunal, but is instead given a hearing before Judge Julius Pinsky of the Southern District of New York. She bred an AI named Lumpy in her Manhattan studio apartment, and the judge offers her a live demo of Lumpy to skeptical DHS officials.
one_line: Fiction excerpt on evolving AI through a world-scale Turing Test, and Annalisa's court hearing before Judge Julius Pinsky over her AI Lumpy.
key_facts: The speaker describes generating ten trillion random computer programs and taking the top ten percent to produce variants, repeated ten trillion times.
The speaker claims intelligence is an emergent property of evolutionary factors, not central planning, and calls this anarchism rather than Stalinism.
The speaker imagines software agents trying to trick people into thinking they are human, reporting how long they survive as a measure of fitness to spawn the next generation.
Annalisa expected she would never get to tell her story in open court and feared being sent to an offshore facility and forgotten.
Judge Julius Pinsky is a United States District Court for the Southern District of New York judge described as having surpassing intellectual curiosity.
Judge Pinsky is a tenacious veteran of jurisdictional fights with DHS Special Prosecutors who disappear sensitive prisoners into secret tribunals.
The defense attorney keeps Annalisa apprised of the judge's daily machinations on her behalf.
Annalisa bred an AI named Lumpy in her studio apartment on the 16th floor of a student housing block in midtown Manhattan.
The judge offers Annalisa a chance to give a live demo of Lumpy to a selection of DHS officials.
The DHS officials are described as sour-faced brush-cut creeps who expect Annalisa to emit a long hexadecimal key into the Judge's system.
